story: Princess Amba was carried off by Bhishma as a bride for his half-brother, then rejected by everyone, including the king she loved. She did fierce penance to Shiva for the power to kill Bhishma, and was reborn as Shikhandi, child of King Drupada, raised as a son. In many tellings a yaksha later exchanged sexes with Shikhandi.
belief: Shikhandi is remembered as the one who brought Bhishma down. Today the story is often discussed as one of the oldest stories of gender change in world literature.
turns: Shikhandi was used as a shield in battle: Bhishma refused to fight someone born a woman, so Arjuna shot him from behind Shikhandi.
facts: Shikhandi was a brother of Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna.
Shikhandi was killed by Ashwatthama in the night raid on the Pandava camp.
The yaksha who exchanged sexes with Shikhandi was named Sthunakarna.
lessons: Who you are isn't decided by how others see you.
A wound can become a purpose.
Your moment may come long after others have forgotten.
more: As Amba, she first asked Parashurama to fight Bhishma; their duel ended without a winner.
Shikhandi fought in the Kurukshetra war as one of the Pandava commanders.
